title: Network Access and Management Methods

header.html: 3.5 Compare and contrast network access and management methods: site-to-site VPN; client-to-site VPN (clientless, split tunnel vs full tunnel); connection methods (SSH, GUI, API, console); jump box or host; in-band vs out-of-band management
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1VPNs

A virtual private network (VPN) creates an encrypted tunnel across an untrusted network.

Type Meaning
Site-to-site VPN Two networks (offices) connected permanently by VPN gateways; users need no client software
Client-to-site (remote access) VPN One user connects to the office network with a VPN client
Clientless VPN Access through a web browser (usually TLS), no software installed, often to specific applications
Full tunnel All the client's traffic goes through the VPN; full inspection and policy, more bandwidth use
Split tunnel Only traffic for company networks goes through the VPN; the rest goes straight to the internet; less load, less control
Exam tip

. Branch offices permanently connected = site-to-site. A traveling employee = client-to-site. Everything must be inspected = full tunnel.

2Management connection methods

Method Meaning
SSH Encrypted command line (port 22); replaces Telnet
GUI A graphical management interface, usually a web page over HTTPS
API Programmatic management (REST), used by automation
Console Direct serial or USB connection to the device; works even with no network; used for initial setup and recovery

3Jump boxes and management paths

Term Meaning
Jump box / jump host A hardened intermediate server admins connect to first, then reach protected devices; one controlled, logged entry point
In-band management Management traffic travels over the production network (SSH, SNMP); fails if the network fails
Out-of-band management A separate path (console server, dedicated management network, cellular modem); works during outages
Exam tip

. "Reach a router when the production network is down" = out-of-band (console or a separate management network). A jump box reduces the attack surface.

Exam tip

. Console works with no network; SSH works over the network; a jump box is the controlled entry point.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Two offices must be connected all the time without any software on user PCs. What fits?

  • AA client-to-site VPN
  • BA site-to-site VPN
  • CA clientless VPN
  • DA captive portal
Show the answer

Answer: B. Site-to-site VPNs link networks through gateways.

S2A traveling employee needs access to internal web applications through a browser with nothing to install. What fits?

  • AA site-to-site VPN
  • BA clientless VPN
  • CA GRE tunnel between offices
  • DPort mirroring
Show the answer

Answer: B. Clientless VPNs use the browser.

S3Security wants all remote-user traffic inspected by the corporate firewall. Which VPN design fits?

  • AA split tunnel
  • BA full tunnel
  • CA clientless tunnel to one application
  • DNo VPN
Show the answer

Answer: B. Full tunnel sends all traffic through the VPN.

S4An engineer must configure a router that has lost all network connectivity. What should the engineer use?

  • AThe console port
  • BSSH over the production network
  • CA web GUI over HTTPS
  • DSNMP
Show the answer

Answer: A. The console works without a network.

S5Administrators must reach servers only through one hardened, logged entry point. What fits?

  • AA split tunnel
  • BA jump box
  • CA hub
  • DA wireless controller
Show the answer

Answer: B. A jump box provides a controlled access path.

S6Which management approach uses a separate network that keeps working during an outage?

  • AIn-band management
  • BOut-of-band management
  • CSNMP polling over production
  • DA web GUI on the production VLAN
Show the answer

Answer: B. Out-of-band uses a separate path.

4.2 Recall questions

R1What is a split tunnel?

Show the answer

Only company traffic uses the VPN; other traffic goes directly to the internet.

R2What does a site-to-site VPN connect?

Show the answer

Two networks, through VPN gateways.

R3Which port does SSH use?

Show the answer

22.

R4What is a console connection?

Show the answer

A direct serial or USB connection that works without a network.

R5What is a jump host?

Show the answer

A hardened intermediate server used to reach protected devices.

R6What is in-band management?

Show the answer

Management over the production network.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
VPN site-to-site (offices), client-to-site (users), clientless (browser); full vs split tunnel
Methods SSH (22), GUI (HTTPS), API, console (no network needed)
Paths jump box (controlled entry), in-band vs out-of-band
